title: Candidate Traceback Interview Lab & Role-Fit Sprint — 14d kit
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, practical playbook for running a 14-day role-fit sprint for late-stage candidates (full-time, contractor-to-perm, and interim ICs). The goal is to quickly validate role fit, reduce time-to-hire, and provide a repeatable Day-0 -> Day-14 assimilation checklist that engineering managers and interview panels can adopt without heavy customization.

Audience:
People Ops (recruiting + L&D), hiring managers, interviewers (eng/product/design), solutions/infra leads responsible for ramping new contributors.

High-level approach (summary):
- Day -2 -> Day 0: Shortlisted candidate accepted an invite for a 2-week role-fit sprint. Paperwork and access handled by People Ops.
- Day 0 -> Day 3: Focused interviews + light onboarding tasks diagnose collaboration fit, coding/workflow baseline, and core domain knowledge.
- Day 4 -> Day 10: Candidate completes 2–3 small scoped tasks in a sandbox repo; paired sessions with future teammates; weekly check-in with hiring manager.
- Day 11 -> Day 14: Final pairing, documentation handoff, and a 1-hour retrospective with panel to synthesize signals and make a hiring decision.

Decision gates (what to assess at each gate):
- Gate A (post-Day 3): Communication & core competency green flags only. Proceed if no major red flags.
- Gate B (post-Day 10): Task delivery + collaborative signals (PR feedback, paired sessions). Proceed to final if task quality meets acceptance criteria.
- Gate C (Day 14): Overall fit, ramp potential, and culture match. Final recommendation: hire / maybe / decline.

Scoring rubric (simple, fast-to-fill):
Panelists score using 1–4 scale (1 = strong red flag, 4 = strong green). Scores should be given for: Technical competency, System design & tradeoffs, Problem decomposition, Collaboration & communication, Learning velocity, Product sense (if applicable).
- Example acceptance: average >= 3.2 and no category with score 1.

Interviewer calibration notes (for the panel lead):
- Keep each live interview to 35–40 minutes max. Use the first 5 minutes to set context & candidate questions.
- If a candidate repeatedly asks for clarifications on ambiguous prompts, mark learning-velocity higher (this is a positive signal if they iterate).
- Distinguish between unfamiliar domain knowledge and inability to reason — penalize the latter.

Sample interview prompts (tailored, short):
- System troubleshooting: "Describe a time you diagnosed a production inference latency spike. What instrumentation did you check first and why?"
- Design micro-problem (20 min): "Sketch a low-cost caching strategy for prefix-heavy LLM requests. Tradeoffs and rollout plan."
- Code exercise (paired, 30 min): small deterministic task from our sandbox repo (parser, KV-cache mini-sim, or batching simulator). Focus on clear tests and incremental design.

Green flags / Red flags (quick heuristics):
- Green flags: asks clarifying Qs early, proposes measurable rollout strategies, gives concise tradeoffs, commits small experiments quickly, shows ownership of postmortems.
- Red flags: repeated finger-pointing, can't justify tradeoffs, no ability to prioritize, uninterested in cross-functional constraints.

Day-0 checklist (People Ops + Hiring manager responsibilities):
- Paperwork: contract/offer preview completed, background check initiated (if required).
- Access: sandbox repo + test infra account created; minimal dataset sanitized and provided; Slack channel + calendar invites done.
- Buddy assigned: peer buddy + onboarding owner for first 14 days.
- Tech setup doc: provide a 1-page start guide (repo layout, run commands, useful tests).

Sandbox task types (pick 2–3 for a 14d sprint):
- Quick bugfix + test (1–3 hrs): shows familiarity with repo/test harness.
- Micro feature (6–12 hrs): small feature that surfaces design choices and tradeoffs.
- Research spike (4–8 hrs): evaluate two approaches and recommend one with evidence.

Task acceptance criteria (apply to each task):
- Completeness: task meets functional spec and includes tests.
- Readability: code and PR have a clear description and rationale.
- Iteration: candidate responds constructively to one round of reviewer feedback.

Rowing the logs (how we capture signals):
- Create a lightweight evidence doc per candidate (People Ops template): short notes per interviewer, links to PRs, timestamps for paired sessions, and a final recommendation paragraph.
- Slack summary: hiring manager posts a 1-paragraph snapshot to #hiring-decision with link to evidence doc.

Manager / Buddy responsibilities during 14d sprint:
- Daily: buddy available for up to 1 hour for context/guidance (not for doing the task).
- Two scheduled pairing sessions (days 4–6 and 8–10) to observe collaboration style.
- End-of-sprint retro: manager, buddy, panel, and candidate in 60-min meeting; use template retro prompts.

Compensation & contracting notes (practical ops):
- Contractors engaged for a 2-week paid sprint (fixed fee). If converted to perm, pay for sprint is applied as credit against first month invoice.
- Use standardized contract language: "trial engagement — evaluation for permanent/extended role" and ensure compliance sign-off from Legal for international hires.

Common pitfalls & mitigations:
- Pitfall: task too large -> candidate misses core signals. Mitigation: split tasks and define strict acceptance criteria.
- Pitfall: interviewers conflate domain expertise with signal of trainability. Mitigation: include explicit learning-velocity rubric item and weigh it equally.
- Pitfall: insufficient onboarding noise -> candidate spends too much time configuring infra. Mitigation: maintain a curated dev sandbox with reproducible test seeds.

Templates & artifacts to attach (links below in linked_artifacts):
- Candidate evidence doc template (one-pager).
- Short tech-setup README (repo runbook).
- Paid-sprint contract sample.

Quick timeline checklist (day-by-day):
- Day -2: Contract & calendar confirmed; sandbox access provisioned.
- Day 0: Kickoff (45 min) — expectations, buddy intro, task pick.
- Day 1–3: 2 short interviews + initial small task. Gate A decision.
- Day 4–7: Work on primary micro-feature; first pairing session.
- Day 8–10: Finish task, iterate on PR, second pairing. Gate B decision.
- Day 11–13: Final polish, documentation handoff, manager feedback loop.
- Day 14: Retro + hiring recommendation. Gate C final decision.

Evidence capture example (short):
- Interviewer: Sofia Alvarez — score: Tech 3, SysDesign 2, Collaboration 4. Notes: "Strong collaborator, hesitated on kernel-level optimizations but proposed pragmatic fallbacks. Recommended follow-up spike on quantization understanding."
- PR: sandbox/prs/123 — reviewer requests: add unit tests; candidate added tests within 48 hours and addressed style feedback.

Communication templates (short snippets):
- Candidate kickoff message: "Welcome! For the next two weeks you'll be working on X in this sandbox. Your buddy is Y and your first pairing is scheduled on Day 5. Reach out in #hiring-[role] for logistics."
- Panel summary to hiring queue: "Candidate: X — Summary: strong collaborator, task met acceptance criteria, learning velocity high. Recommendation: move to offer."

Post-hire short ramp (if hired):
- 30/60/90 micro-plan that absorbs the sprint artifacts: treat sprint tasks as first-week deliverables, buddy continues weekly check-ins for 30 days, and manager sets three measurable goals for 60/90.

Open questions for People Ops team to finalize before wider rollout:
- Standard paid-sprint fee by role band? (Finance input required)
- Legal-approved language for international trial engagements.
- Which hiring panels must include a diversity & inclusion observer for bias mitigation?

Notes / future improvements backlog (working list):
- Shorten Day 0 kickoff to 30 min and publish a sample agenda.
- Build small automated infra to seed sandbox test data and a reproducible benchmarking harness.
- Create a lightweight rubric card in Greenhouse/ATS for rapid scoring.

Author: Maya Chen (People Ops) — draft for review by Recruiting & Eng managers.
